newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP sees A$4.5 bln 97/8 capital expenditure.
newsitem.headline: BHP sees A$4.5 bln 97/8 capital expenditure.

text.p: Australia's The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) on Monday said it planned capital expenditure, including exploration, of A$4.5 billion in the year ending May 31, 1998.
BHP, Australia's largest listed company, said earlier it was currently spending A$4 billion on new investments in Australia, with A$1 billion in its steel sector.

"We have four billion (dollars) of new projects currently underway in Australia in all business groups in all mainland states, and about one billion of that is in steel," BHP Managing Director John Prescott told a briefing seminar.
"About 4,000 BHP employees were working on new projects in Australia," Prescott said.
BHP on Friday announced a 60.8 percent fall in net profit of A$410 million for the year to May 31, 1997, after booking abnormal losses totalling more than A$1 billion before tax.
The abnormal losses included a write-down in some North American copper assets of A$550 million, a writedown in steel assets of A$220 million and a writedown in minerals assets of A$189 million.
